title: Computational thinking: instructions, patterns and algorithms
audience: a child in grades K–5 working with an adult helper who reads along
purpose: Follow and write exact step-by-step instructions, spot patterns, use loops and choices, find and fix bugs, break big jobs into small steps, and see how computers store information as numbers, all without a computer.

weeks.6: Breaking big jobs into small steps

blocks.deliverable: Write instructions for a partner to draw a shape.
Shorten a long set of instructions with a loop.
Find and fix the bug in three sets of instructions.
Week 7 midterm; sort ten cards by a rule and explain the rule.
Count from 0 to 31 with five binary cards.
Make a poster of three rules for staying safe online.
Submit the project; take an unseen 30 minute final in week 14.

project: Robot maze: draw a maze on grid paper, write step-by-step instructions with loops and if-then choices that guide a "robot" partner to the treasure, test them, fix the bugs, and present the final program.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
